picked.t: Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 to connect FDI enterprises with business opportunities
picked.body: The half-day event, scheduled from 8:30 a.m. to noon at Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection, will host discussions covering investment policies, tax regulations, economic trends and financial market developments. The agenda will also include pre-arranged business meetings connecting companies with potential service providers. Speakers will examine Vietnam's investment policies and business environment, including changes to corporate income tax, value-added tax and personal income tax, as well as tax administration, investment incentives and support policies. Other topics will include Vietnam's economic outlook, global developments, international trade, interest rates, foreign exchange movements and investment flows. The three speakers are Bui Thu Thuy, deputy director of the Foreign Investment Agency under the Ministry of Finance; Nguyen Thi Cuc, president of the Vietnam Tax Consultants' Association and former deputy director general of the General Department of , Ministry of Finance; and economist Nguyen Xuan Thanh. The forum will also feature a Business Matching program, with meetings arranged in advance based on participants' cooperation needs. The program will connect FDI enterprises with providers of logistics, legal advisory, investment consulting, accounting and finance, and general contracting services. Participants will be able to assess potential partners and explore services relevant to their operations and expansion plans. VietinBank said the forum is part of its efforts to support FDI enterprises beyond conventional banking services, using its domestic and international network to connect businesses with expertise and potential partners. The bank provides FDI clients with working capital financing, cash management, domestic and international payments, and trade finance. It also offers market and policy updates and connections with specialists and advisory organizations. Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 – Vietnam Investment and Business Networking Forum Date: Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026 Time: 8:30 a.m. - noon Venue: Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection, 720A Dien Bien Phu Street, Vinhomes Tan Cang, Thanh My Tay Ward, Ho Chi Minh City Participants: FDI enterprises, investors, and domestic and international organizations Businesses interested in attending Vietnam Connect Forum 2026 or participating in Business Matching can register or submit their partnership requests directly at the nearest VietinBank branch or transaction office, or through the following channels: Email: fdi@vietinbank.vn Hotline: 1900 558 886

picked.t: Vietnam tourism website is 2nd busiest in Southeast Asia after Singapore
picked.body: VisitSingapore.com had nearly 424,000 visits, up 6%, according to digital analytics platform Similarweb. Thailand's Tourismthailand.org was third with around 338,000 visits, down 20% from the previous month. Vietnam.travel also recorded stronger visitor engagement than its regional counterparts, with visitors spending an average of 53 seconds on the website, compared with 44 seconds on Singapore's and 43 seconds on Thailand's portals. The Vietnamese website averaged 1.92 pages viewed per visit as against 1.63 for VisitSingapore.com and 1.76 for Tourismthailand.org. International visitors accounted for nearly 91% of Vietnam.travel's traffic, compared with 86% for Singapore and 62% for Thailand. The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism said Vietnam.travel is undergoing upgrades to its interface, content and technology to better support international visitors throughout their trips in the country. The website, which initially offered content only in English, now has 10 more languages: Japanese, Chinese, Korean, French, German, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, and Thai. It covers nature, culture, heritage, islands and coastal destinations, cuisine, leisure, and travel experiences. The platform is also being developed to incorporate services such as tour searches, flight bookings, hotel reservations, attraction tickets, transportation, eSIMs, and golf course access. Visitors will be able to choose services, submit booking requests, and make online payments through these integrated connections. Artificial intelligence is on the cards to support conversational translation, information searches, travel consultations, and personalized itinerary planning based on individual preferences. The authority aims to transform Vietnam.travel from a destination information website into a platform connecting international visitors with local destinations, domestic businesses, and service providers. The development is being carried out in phases, depending on progress in partner integration, data standardization, system testing, and service rollout.

picked.t: Vietnamese hospital receives Japanese cell therapy technology for cancer and chronic disease treatment
picked.body: Vietnam's Tam Anh General Hospital Group and Japan's Grandsoul Medical Group have completed the transfer of natural killer (NK) immune cell and mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) technologies, marking a new step in medical cooperation between the two countries. Developed by the Grandsoul Research Institute for Immunology in Nara, Japan, two technologies being transferred to Tam Anh hospital are autologous NK therapy, and autologous MSC therapy. The first one includes the protocols of cell activation, expansion, evaluation and preparation for cancer treatment, while the second includes adipose tissue processing, cell isolation, expansion and evaluation. The completion of the technology transfer was announced on Nov. 9 during a visit to Japan by a high-level Vietnamese delegation from Nov. 8 to 11. The ceremony was witnessed by Party General Secretary and President To Lam and senior officials from both countries. Tam Anh is one of the first institutions in Vietnam selected, on an exclusive basis, for the comprehensive transfer of these core technologies from leading Japanese group Grandsoul. The transfer opens up new opportunities for treatment of cancer and chronic diseases and improving the health of people in Vietnam. Mastering cell therapy (stem cells and immune cells) to treat cancer, chronic diseases and intractable diseases is a national strategy approved by the Government for implementation from 2026 to 2030. This comprehensive, in-depth transfer is good news, as it makes this the first strategic technology realized ahead of schedule in Vietnam. According to Tam Anh , the technologies are intended for use across its five facilities in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, which together handle more than 10,000 patient visits daily. NK cells are lymphocytes that belong to the innate immune system and act as rapid first-line defense against abnormal cells, including cancer cells. Under the transferred technology, immune cells are collected from a patient's blood, isolated and cultured under specialized conditions to increase their numbers and activate their functions before being infused back into the patient. NK cell-based therapies are being investigated for several cancers, including breast, lung, stomach, bladder, kidney and colorectal cancers. Their effectiveness and appropriate use, however, depend on the cancer type, treatment and available clinical evidence. Ta Thanh Van, chairman of the Professional Council of Tam Anh General Hospital for Regenerative Medicine and Cell Therapy in Hanoi, said NK cell therapy could provide an additional option alongside surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy and targeted therapy. The second technology involves MSCs derived from a patient's own adipose tissue. The cells are isolated, processed and cultured before being prepared for use in the same patient. MSCs have been well-studied for their ability to regulate immune responses and support tissue repair. They have demonstrated therapeutic potential for cardiovascular and neurological conditions, including stroke and dementia, as well as diabetes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and dermatological treatments. Many of these applications remain under clinical investigation, and their effectiveness and regulatory status vary by condition. Before the transfer, Japanese specialists visited Tam Anh to assess its facilities, laboratories and cell-processing procedures. The hospital said the assessment found that its infrastructure and processes met the technical requirements. Matsuo Yoshinobu, a senior technology specialist at the Grandsoul Nara Institute of Immunology Research, said Tam Anh had established the infrastructure, workforce and quality-control procedures needed to receive the technologies. "We are ready to work together to develop regenerative medicine in Vietnam safely, with treatment effectiveness and patient safety as our top priorities," he said. Van said the hospital had invested in specialized equipment, skilled personnel and international research partnerships to prepare for the transfer. Tam Anh established a tissue and umbilical cord blood bank, licensed by Vietnam's Ministry of Health in 2019 before developing its Center for Regenerative Medicine and Cell Therapy. The hospital has also invested in advanced diagnostic and treatment equipment, including CT and 3-Tesla MRI scanners, PET/CT imaging and molecular diagnostics. It operates two Da Vinci Xi robotic surgical systems and reports having performed more than 600 robotic procedures. Its cancer services include chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy and multidisciplinary treatment. A Mevion S250-FIT proton therapy system from the U.S., valued at nearly VND2 trillion (US$78.2 million), is being installed ahead of planned operation. According to Tam Anh, the technology transfer will help it develop domestic capabilities in cell isolation, cell culture and preparation under standards established by its Japanese partner. picked.t: HCMC plans logistics hub network across 10 locations
picked.body: The 10 locations planned are Cat Lai, Long Binh, Linh Trung, Saigon Hi-Tech Park, Tan Kien, Hiep Phuoc, Cu Chi, Hoc Mon, Binh Khanh and the area around Tan Son Nhat International Airport. The plan is part of a resolution on free trade zones and integrated logistics zones approved by the municipal People's Council on Oct. 30. The network will connect industrial parks and production areas with ports, airports and markets. Goods will be consolidated, sorted, stored, processed and transferred at the hubs before reaching their destinations. The city expects the system to reduce unnecessary freight movements, lower transport costs and limit heavy truck traffic in densely populated areas. Following its merger with Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces, HCMC is home to an estimated 60-70% of Vietnam's logistics companies, according to the municipal administration. More than 15,300 businesses operate in logistics, transport, warehousing, bonded storage, seaport services and related sectors across the expanded city. However, the sector faces challenges involving operating costs, land use and infrastructure connectivity. Warehouses are scattered and often small, while large distribution centers and integrated logistics hubs remain limited. Freight transport relies heavily on roads, with inadequate connections among road, inland waterway, rail, seaport and air networks. Logistics costs account for an estimated 16-17% of Vietnam's GDP, while transportation makes up 50-70% of total logistics expenses, depending on the industry and transport mode. For seafood and agricultural products, logistics can represent 20-25% of total costs, affecting competitiveness. Demand for freight services is expected to rise as HCMC expands its industrial and transport infrastructure. The city's master plan provides for 105 export processing and industrial zones covering about 50,288 hectares. Major facilities, including the Cai Mep-Thi Vai port complex, the planned Can Gio International Transshipment Port, Tan Son Nhat International Airport and Long Thanh International Airport, are also expected to increase cargo volumes and demand for domestic and international freight services. The proposed hubs will integrate logistics functions, improve the use of transport infrastructure and reduce heavy freight traffic through urban areas. The city also plans to promote digital management, automation and environmentally sustainable logistics practices. Investment incentives for integrated logistics zones Under the resolution, HCMC will develop two types of integrated logistics zones: facilities within free trade zones and independent facilities outside them. The approval process, from consultation with relevant authorities to licensing, must not exceed 30 days. Investors developing infrastructure for these zones will be eligible for land rental exemptions and interest rate support from the municipal budget for up to seven years. Separately, HCMC plans to establish a free trade zone covering more than 4,165 hectares near Cai Mep Ha port. The zone will include logistics, industrial production, trade and services, education and training, research and development, digital technology facilities, data centers and non-tariff areas. The municipal administration said the free trade zone and integrated logistics zones would serve complementary roles. The former is intended to attract investment in manufacturing, trade, import-export activities and value-added services, while the latter will provide facilities for storing, processing, distributing and transferring goods across the city's transport network.

picked.t: Motion sickness fuels demand for long-distance motorbike taxis
picked.body: On Nov. 3, Ly Van Thanh, 24, traveled from Bac Ninh to Lao Cai Province to collect a female passenger heading to Hanoi. She paid more than VND2 million (US$80) for the 238-kilometer journey. "Every single day I get three to four booking requests, but I only take one to stay healthy and sharp," Thanh says. Thanh previously worked for app-based ride-hailing services, grinding 16 to 18 hours daily for meager returns of VND4,000 to VND5,000 per kilometer. In early 2026, realizing that severe motion sickness left many travelers eager to pay a premium for long-distance motorcycle travel across provinces, he walked away from the gig platforms to work for himself. He spent over VND10 million to upgrade his bike, outfitting it with high-traction tires, stronger shock absorbers, auxiliary headlights, heavy-duty cargo racks, and a custom-cushioned seat. In March, he took on his maiden private trip from the port city of Hai Phong to Hanoi. Along the route, he filmed his rides and shared them on social media. By May, a clip documenting a 200-kilometer run from Hai Phong to Quang Ninh racked up more than 350,000 views. From that point on, inquiries have been pouring in nonstop, and pushed his operational range to 400 to 500 kilometers across the rugged northern highlands. On a 412-kilometer haul once from Hai Phong to Son La, he rode straight between 7 p.m. to 6 a.m the next day. Every 100 kilometers, he made a point of stopping so that both he and his passenger could grab a bite and rest. "Early on, finishing a marathon haul like that would leave me knocked out for a day or two," he says. "Over time, my body adjusted; now I know my exact physical endurance limits and scout every route in detail before setting off." The business comes with some hazards, nevertheless. Once, he rode all the way from Hai Phong to Hanoi to pick up a traveler bound for the northwestern mountains, only to have the client cancel on arrival. In early September, he carried a passenger over 300 kilometers from Phu Tho up to Mu Cang Chai, and he only collected an advance of VND400,000. Having learned the hard way, he now has clear policies: clients must wire a 50% deposit upfront, no night trips or runs into deep wilderness with male passengers, and bookings are never subcontracted. "Clients book me because they trust my personal track record," he points out. "Passing clients off to a total stranger puts them in harm's way." Since pivoting fully into interprovincial motorcycle hires, Thanh has doubled or tripled the income he made on ride-hailing apps. Women struggling with acute motion sickness make up 95% of his clientele, and his personal social media channels have drawn 118,000 followers. Xuan Anh, 29, based in Ninh Binh Province has been offering the same service for the last three months, and also witnessed an explosion in long-haul demand. Xuan Anh charges VND8,000 per kilometer plus a VND3,000 surcharge per kilometer when picking up passengers in remote provinces. "The main advantage is keeping every dong without paying a cut to tech platforms," he says. "Clients willingly pay far more than conventional motorcycle taxis because the service is tailored, comfortable, and reliable." To handle demanding routes, Xuan Anh taught himself how to repair motorcycles, asks for a 70% deposit, and declines late-night trips with men. More than 80% of his clientele consists of women with motion sickness or people handling urgent business who need flexible, door-to-door transit. A smaller subset simply hires him to experience scenic, open-air motorcycle touring. The dread of motion sickness has turned long-distance motorcycle trips from the occasional one by drivers like Ly Van Thanh and Xuan Anh into a booming transport niche. Across social media feeds, dozens of independent drivers now advertise private, on-demand cross-country journeys. Examining the trend, economist Huynh Thanh Dien in Ho Chi Minh City notes that gig workers walking away from algorithmic platforms with their rigid pricing rules and policy constraints to cultivate personal brands and direct client followings represents a logical evolution in the freelance economy. "Still, this isn't a game everyone can play." Making a viable living out of this trade requires savvy self-marketing skills, an impeccable long-term reputation, cardiovascular stamina, a rock-solid vehicle, and quick instincts for dealing with roadside trouble. Looking ahead, both Thanh and Anh believe the market has enormous untapped potential as consumer appetite for personalized travel keeps expanding. But both point to an uncompromising golden rule for anyone wanting to jump in: respect every mile of the road, inspect your machine without cutting corners, and place rider and passenger safety above everything else. picked.t: Vietnamese single mother raises two children through travel and self-study
picked.body: At 6 a.m. on an early November morning, inside a mobile home parked in Son Tra Ward in Da Nang, Thi urged her daughter, Nhu Y, 14, to log into her online sewing class. While her daughter was in class, she phoned her son, Duy Thanh, to ask about his life in the dormitory of Vietnamese-German University in HCMC. In early September, he was admitted to the university’s electrical and computer engineering program on the strength of a GED certificate (equivalent to a U.S. high school diploma), an IELTS score of 7.5, and an SAT score of 1,390. These results came from Thanh’s five years of self-study. The family's nomadic life began following a tragedy in 2020. At the time, the HCMC native was working as an accountant while her husband was a bus driver. He was diagnosed with cancer and passed away within two months. Having lost her income after taking time off to care for her husband, she moved back to her mother's house with her two children, selling yogurt at the local market and crocheting to make ends meet. After his father's passing, Thanh, then 12 years old, became addicted to video games. Meanwhile, the memory of her husband's cancer made Thi pay greater attention to their living environment and food sources. She began researching in online communities of people who had left the city for the countryside By 2021, Thi sold her house and land, and moved her two children from HCMC to a house borrowed from a friend in Cu M’gar Commune in the central Dak Lak Province. Living alongside the Ede ethnic minority people, she noticed local children often accompanied their parents to the fields in the morning and attended school in the afternoon, yet remained healthy, had strong immune systems, and were helpful to others. This observation prompted her to redesign her children's education. Taking advantage of the shift to online schooling during the Covid-19 pandemic, she enrolled her two children in homeschooling under the United States’ Acellus program, which cost US$25 per month. All subjects were taught in English. To tackle her son's gaming addiction, she handed him a hoe to till the soil and clear weeds. She involved both children in tasks such as painting and repairing abandoned houses and building cabinets. Every day, Thanh went out with friends to play in the rain and splash around in streams, and helped tend fields of okra, scallions, cilantro, and radishes. Thanks to the increased outdoor physical activity, he spent significantly less time on his computer. Each month, she took her children to agricultural workshops where they learned to saw bamboo to build trellises for sponge gourds, prepare soil for growing vegetables, and study clean agriculture models, how biomass stoves work, and how to recycle biochar byproducts. To earn an income, Thi sold farm produce online and referred guests to homestays. Their nomadic life began when the family started relocating every three to six months, moving through places such as Hue, Da Nang, Binh Dinh Province, and Tuy An Nam Commune in Dak Lak Province. In mid-2023, while renting a home near the coast of Tuy An Nam, she sent Thanh to help out at Phuoc Luu’s coffee shop in Lo Village to gain real-world experience. Over three months, he waited tables, looked after the dogs, tended the garden, and learned how to make drinks. Outside of work hours, Thanh went swimming in the ocean with local children and studied on his computer in the evening. When Luu opened a community bookstore next to the coffee shop, Thanh helped clean, set up the premises, and plant vegetables and flowers with the younger kids. His strong English skills allowed him to serve foreign customers. He also joined trekking, camping, and waterfall expeditions, helping carry gear, cook meals, take photos, and support others. "The boy completely changed after that summer, becoming proactive, lively, and outgoing," Luu says. To make moving easier, in early 2025, Thi purchased and renovated an old mobile home for VND800 million. The shower area was downsized to make room for a kitchen cabinet and a washing machine. Inside this vehicle, Nhu Y has a dedicated corner for sewing, embroidery, and playing the violin. Both her children are now in charge of their own study schedules. Thi only monitors the schedules and uses an app to track the total hours they study each day.. "There is no single best educational environment for everyone, only an environment that fits each child," Thi says about her family's five-year journey.

picked.t: 베트남, 하노이 노이바이공항 ‘국제선 전노선’ 자빈공항 이전 추진…2029~2030년
picked.body: 베트남 하노이 노이바이국제공항 2터미널. (사진=노이바이공항) 베트남이 수도 하노이에 위치한 노이바이(Noi Bai) 국제공항에서 운항 중인 국제선을 박닌(Bac Ninh)에 건설 중인 자빈(Gia Binh) 국제공항으로 모두 이전하는 계획을 검토하고 있다. 하노이시에 따르면, 지난 9일 부 다이 탕(Vu Dai Thang) 하노이시 인민위원장이 주재한 회의에서는 노이바이공항의 국제선 이전안과 함께 두 공항과 도심 간 철도 연결 방안이 중점적으로 논의됐다. 이날 회의에는 하노이시 지도부 외 부이 쑤언 융(Bui Xuan Dung) 건설부 차관과 응우옌 만 꾸옌(Nguyen Manh Quyen) 흥옌성(Hung Yen) 인민위원장 등이 참석했다. 융 차관은 “정부는 자빈국제공항 운영계획 연구를 관련 기관에 지시한 상태로, 여기에는 노이바이공항의 국제선 전(全) 노선을 자빈공항으로 이전하는 가능성 검토 방안도 포함돼 있다”고 밝혔다. 해당 계획이 현실화하면, 2029~2030년 노이바이공항에서는 국내선과 일부 국제선이 운항될 예정이다. 융 차관은 이어 “노이바이공항은 2030년까지 연간 여객 5,000만 명을 처리하고 2050년에는 처리 능력이 1억 명에 이를 것으로 전망된다. 하노이 남쪽의 제2공항을 건설하는 방안은 수도 장기발전계획에 따라 이후 단계에서 추진될 계획”이라고 덧붙였다. 철도 노선과 관련, 융 차관은 노이바이공항과 자빈공항을 잇는 도시철도 노선과 자빈공항에서 지아럼역(Gia Lam)을 거쳐 도심에 이르는 최단 철도 노선 연구를 하노이시에 주문했다. 그는 지아럼역은 국철과 지역 철도, 특수철도 및 도시철도망이 만나는 주요 환승역으로 개발하고, 다른 주요 도시철도역과 이어지는 잠재적인 노선의 연구를 주문했다. 이번 도시철도 계획은 하노이 도심에서 각 공항으로의 이동 시간을 약 30~45분 수준으로 단축하는 것을 목표로 한 것으로, 이를 위해 정차역을 최소화한 급행열차 도입도 고려되고 있다. 이 밖에도 융 차관은 하노이와 흥옌성, 박닌을 잇는 광역 철도망 건설을 검토해 국가철도망과의 통합을 도모하고, 우선적으로 투자해야 할 구간을 선정하고, 하노이 도심에서 노이바이공항 북쪽으로 이어지는 별도 노선의 연구를 하노이시에 지시하고, 베트남철도청에는 관계 기관 및 지방당국과 협력을 통해 해당 제안들을 신속히 검토하고 확정할 것을 지시했다. 탕 위원장 또한 지아럼역을 국철과 고속철도, 도시철도가 만나는 주요 환승 거점으로 개발하자는 방안에 동의했다. 그는 “최근 승인된 하노이 100년 마스터플랜은 도심에 집중하지 않고, 주요 개발 거점과 교통 허브를 철도로 잇는 다핵 도시 모델을 기반으로 하고 있다. 이미 승인된 계획의 대규모 수정을 피하기 위해 국철 1호선의 북남 노선은 그대로 유지하되, 지아럼역 일대와 도심을 잇고, 동쪽으로 자빈공항까지 이어지는 지선 개발을 추가로 검토할 수 있다”고 밝혔다. 탕 위원장은 “해당 계획안은 목적지 간 이동거리를 줄이되, 승인된 철도 계획이나 진행 중인 사업을 근본적으로 바꾸지 않는 절충안으로, 이를 통해 자빈공항과 노이바이공항을 직접 연결하는 철도망이 구축될 경우, 지아빈공항을 통해 도착한 국제선 여객이 철도를 이용해 노이바이공항으로 이동해 국내선으로 환승할 수 있고, 그 반대의 경우도 가능하다”며 “이러한 계획들은 정부 제출전 실현 가능성과 마스터플랜과의 일치성을 추가적으로 연구할 필요가 있다”고 덧붙였다. 현재 하노이에서 43km 떨어진 박닌시에서 건설 중인 자빈공항은 전체 부지 면적만 약 1,960헥타르로, 완공 시 규모면에서 남부 동나이시의 5,000헥타르 롱탄국제공항(Long Thanh)에 이어 베트남 2위 공항에 오르게 된다. 사업비 75억 달러 규모의 자빈공항은 대형기 수용이 가능한 국제민간항공기구(ICAO) 코드 4F 기준으로 설계됐다. 지난해 8월 착공된 이 공항은 2027년 아시아태평양경제협력체(APEC) 정상회의 개최 시기에 맞춰 완공을 목표로 한다. 자빈공항은 2030년 연간 여객 3,000만 명과 화물 160만 톤, 2050년에는 여객 5,000만 명과 화물 250만 톤을 처리할 수 있는 수준으로 확장이 진행될 예정이다.

Foreign investors also contributed more than $3.6 billion to domestic businesses through capital contributions and share purchases. Nguyen Loc Ha, vice chairman of the HCMC People's Committee, said the city had attracted several major projects, including the Can Gio International Transshipment Port, with investment exceeding $4.9 billion, and a $2.1 billion AI Factory data center project. "This is a positive sign of investors' interest and confidence in the city," he said at the Fortune Southeast Asia 500 Summit in HCMC. Foreign investment has increased following the city's merger with Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau provinces. The expanded city has more than 14 million residents and contributes approximately 23.5% of Vietnam's gross domestic product. Ha said the city has strengths in finance, trade, services and high-tech manufacturing, as well as access to international shipping routes through the Cai Mep-Thi Vai deepwater port complex. HCMC is focusing on four areas to attract more investment: improving institutions and long-term planning; linking foreign investors with domestic supply chains; developing infrastructure and growth drivers such as the international financial center, free trade zones, logistics, AI and automation; and improving public services, transparency and support for businesses. The city's economy also recorded growth in several areas during the first 10 months of the year. Industrial production rose 11% year-on-year, exports increased 10.9%, and retail sales of goods and consumer services grew 14.7%. Public investment disbursement exceeded VND114.4 trillion ($4.48 billion), equivalent to 77.5% of the annual plan. However, rising global fuel prices contributed to inflationary pressure, with the city's consumer price index increasing by an average of 4.78% during the period. Business activity remained challenging. From the beginning of the year through Oct. 20, HCMC licensed more than 44,700 new businesses with combined registered capital of VND365.185 trillion. The number of newly established businesses fell 6% year-on-year, while their registered capital dropped 58.1%.

picked.t: 호치민시, ‘외국인투자’ 유치 급증세…10월 기준 190억 달러 돌파 전년동기比 4.3배↑
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시의 중심업무지구. 올 들어 베트남 호치민시의 외국인직접투자(FDI) 유치액이 200억 달러에 육박하는 등 큰 폭의 증가세를 보이고 있다. 호치민시 통계국에 따르면, 10월 기준 FDI 유치액은 누계 191억 달러를 기록했다. 지난해 같은 기간과 비교하면 4.2배 급증한 수준이다. 이는 같은 기간 베트남 전체 FDI 유치액인 548억5,000만 달러의 약 35%에 달하는 것으로, 껀저국제환적항과 같은 대규모 프로젝트가 잇따른 데 따른 영향이다. 형태별 투자 유치 규모는 신규 사업이 1,726건, 약 98억 달러로 가장 많았고, 추가 투자 및 증자가 57억 달러, 출자 및 지분 매입이 36억 달러 상당을 기록했다. 이와 관련하여, 응우옌 록 하(Nguyen Loc Ha) 호치민시 인민위원회 부위원장은 최근 관내에서 열린 한 투자 행사에서 “올해 들어 49억여 달러 규모 껀저국제환적항과 21억 달러 규모 AI팩토리데이터센터 등 대규모 프로젝트가 잇따라 유치되며 외국 자본 유치액이 큰 폭으로 늘고 있다”며 “이는 호치민시에 대한 투자자의 관심과 신뢰를 보여주는 긍정적인 신호”라고 평가했다. 그는 이어 “호치민시는 금융·상업·서비스·첨단 산업에 더해 국제 해상 운송로와 직접 연결되는 까이멥-티바이심해항(Cai Mep-Thi Vai port) 클러스터까지 여러 분야에서 강력한 경쟁력을 갖추고 있다”며 “호치민시는 외국 자본 유치를 위해 △제도 정비 및 장기계획 수립 △국내 공급망 연계 △인프라 확충 △국제금융센터·자유무역지대·인공지능(AI) 및 자동화 등 신성장동력 발굴 등 4가지 핵심 분야에 주력하고 있으며, 이와 동시에 서비스 품질 향상과 정보 투명성 제고, 기업 애로사항 해소 등에도 많은 노력을 기울이고 있다”고 덧붙였다. 호치민시의 FDI 유치액은 지난해 빈즈엉성·바리아붕따우성과의 통폐합 뒤 빠른 속도로 늘고 있다. 행정구역 통폐합 뒤 정주인구 1,400만여 명의 대도시로 거듭난 호치민시는 현재 베트남 국내총생산(GDP)의 23.5%를 담당하는 핵심 성장 동력으로서 그 지위를 공고히 하고 있다. 외국인 투자 유치 외 올 들어 호치민시는 많은 경제지표에서 긍정적인 성과가 나타나고 있다. 10월 기준 산업생산지수(IIP)는 전년 동기 대비 11% 증가했고, 수출액은 10.9% 늘었다. 또한 공공투자 집행액은 114조4,000억 동(44억7,180만여 달러)을 넘어 연간 목표의 77.5%에 도달했으며, 소매판매도 14.7% 증가하며 두 자릿수 성장세를 이어갔다. 다만 고물가로 인해 구매력은 다소 제한되는 모습을 보였다. 10월 기준 호치민시의 소비자물가지수(CPI)는 평균 4.78% 올랐는데, 국제 유가 상승에 따른 연료 가격 상승이 주범으로 풀이된다. 또한 지난달 20일 기준 호치민시에 신설된 법인 수는 4만4,700여 개, 등록자본금은 365조1,850억 동(약 142억7,480만 달러)으로 전년 동기 대비 6%, 58.1% 각각 감소하는 등 사업 환경에서도 어려움이 지속적으로 관측됐다.

picked.t: Hundreds of young patients attend Sun of Hope festival in Hanoi
picked.body: Hundreds of pediatric patients took part in the Sun of Hope festival at Hanoi Children's Hospital on Nov. 7, where organizers arranged games, performances and gifts to provide entertainment for children undergoing treatment. The event was organized by Hope Foundation in coordination with the hospital and MUFG Bank Ltd.'s Hanoi Branch. Activity booths across the hospital grounds offered statue painting, sand art, ring toss and balloon twisting, alongside a food area. The program aimed to give children a recreational space outside hospital wards and help ease the stress associated with prolonged treatment. Le Thi Thuy, 42, who attended with her son, said the activities offered them a welcome break from hospital treatment. Her 13-year-old son, Phi Ngoc Bao, has kidney failure and congenital cerebral palsy and cannot walk independently. The family has been coming to the hospital for treatment three times a week since May. "Today I brought him down to the lobby earlier than usual to watch the magic show. These activities help him forget some of the pain after dialysis," Thuy said. As part of the event, MUFG Bank's Hanoi Branch, through Hope Foundation, donated an indoor playground, five trees and six electric syringe pumps to the hospital, as well as hundreds of gifts for patients. The sponsorship was valued at VND250 million (US$9,770). Yohei Ota, deputy general manager of MUFG Bank's Hanoi Branch, said the bank hoped to make practical contributions to the community. "We are very honored to accompany Hope Foundation and Hanoi Children's Hospital in bringing joy and sharing to the children and families with children undergoing treatment at the hospital," he said. Dr. Ngo Quang Hung, director of Hanoi Children's Hospital, said the support would help improve hospital facilities and ease the psychological burden on patients' families. "Community sharing embodies the philosophy we pursue - making every effort so that fewer children need to come to the hospital," he said. Support for pediatric patients is part of Hope Foundation's Sun of Hope program, launched in 2021. The program has supported treatment for more than 3,500 young patients and provided emotional support to thousands of others. Readers can support children through the Sun of Hope program .
